quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur: Honeywell Technologies' first quarter as a standalone pure-play automation company (after the aerospace spin-off). CFO Mike Stepniak: third-quarter sales grew seven percent organically with strength across all segments (CEO Vimal Kapur: above the high end of the targets unveiled at Investor Day in June). Process Automation & Technology sales grew eight percent organically - double-digit growth in projects (project sales up 14% on LNG and petrochemical backlog conversion) and a return to growth in aftermarket, led by refining catalyst demand; its margin contracted as expected on project mix and dilution from the acquired Johnson Matthey Catalyst Technologies business. Building Automation grew eight percent organically, its eighth straight quarter of high single-digit growth (products up 11% organically, led by fire and security; solutions up four percent, driven by services; segment margin up another 30 basis points to 27%). Industrial Automation organic sales were up four percent (double-digit growth in solutions, principally industrial measurement and utilities; product sales roughly flat as sensing and industrial measurement demand was offset by industry-wide deferrals in utility meter deployments; price and productivity drove 350 basis points of margin expansion). Segment profit grew 23% and segment margin expanded 370 basis points to 21.3%; adjusted EPS $2.27, up 34%; free cash flow up 15% to roughly $690 million, with conversion of 95%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 organic sales growth seven percent; segment margin 21.3% (up 370 basis points); adjusted EPS $2.27 (up 34%); free cash flow roughly $690 million (up 15%)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur: third-quarter short-cycle orders grew eight percent excluding divestitures, led by industrial and building automation (sensing and measurement; double-digit growth in Building Automation product businesses); orders in the data center vertical were up over 100%; strong refining Catalyst Technologies demand; regional strength in India, the Middle East and Africa. Process Automation & Technology faced a tough comparison with two strategic low carbon energy and LNG awards in the third and fourth quarter of 2025 of $700 million each; excluding the Q3 award last year, total company orders were up three percent organically. Book-to-bill was 1.0 and ending backlog was nearly $19 billion, up seven percent excluding divestitures; PA&T backlog is over 10% higher than a year ago (wins across LNG, refining and petrochemicals and low-carbon energy), with over $1 billion in process technology orders since quarter one of 2026. CFO Mike Stepniak: third-quarter Industrial Automation core orders were up 15%, taking the business into next year with probably the best backlog it has seen in over five years. CEO: fourth-quarter orders are expected to grow in the high single-digit range excluding last year's large LNG award; the first three weeks of October have been trending on and above expectations.
quarterly_data.figure: ending backlog nearly $19 billion (up seven percent excluding divestitures); book-to-bill 1.0; orders up three percent organically excluding last year's Q3 award; data center vertical orders up over 100%; Industrial Automation core orders up 15%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak: Honeywell raised its full-year 2026 organic growth, adjusted EPS and free cash flow guidance and tightened margin guidance around the previous high end - organic growth now four percent-five percent (previously three percent-four percent), with five percent-six percent organic growth expected in the fourth quarter (continued strength in Building Automation, high single-digit growth in Process Automation & Technology on project backlog conversion and higher Catalyst Technologies volumes); full-year segment margin at the high end of the range at 20.5% and approximately 22% in the fourth quarter (Industrial Automation 22%, Building Automation expanding margins 70 - 90 basis points, Process Automation & Technology around 21.5%); adjusted EPS $8.40-$8.45, a $0.23 improvement at the midpoint with the low end above the previous high end, for full-year earnings growth of approximately 30%; free cash flow guidance up $100 million to $2.1 billion, with conversion expected above 100% in the fourth quarter. CFO on Q4: 'As we stand today, we are probably on the higher end of the five percent.' CEO Vimal Kapur: 2027 organic growth is expected to be at or above the long-term growth algorithm; he remains 'very confident on performing at upper end of our four percent-six percent guide' and says Honeywell is 'on a road to deliver $12 or better', the 2029 target set at Investor Day (all organic); 2027 guidance will come in February.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 organic growth four percent-five percent (from three percent-four percent); Q4 organic growth five percent-six percent; segment margin 20.5% (Q4 approximately 22%); adjusted EPS $8.40-$8.45; free cash flow $2.1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur on project execution and capacity: labor shortages are not a concern because a large part of the backlog is outside North America (the LNG backlog is in North America) - 'In case of LNG, we build our own equipment in our own factory, and we have enough capacity to fulfill all our backlogs'; construction labor shortages are a trend but are not driving any visible impact on revenue execution. On refining, deferrals or higher uptime by U.S. refiners mean work that needs a shutdown (replacing a Sundyne pump, refurbishing a catalyst) is moving right - 'it's not a lost demand', rather pent-up demand that will eventually show up - while automation work that can be done online (cybersecurity hardening, control-system migration) is protected.

CEO Vimal Kapur on Industrial Automation metering: Honeywell has introduced very new technology for gas meters and water meters; gas meters, unlike electricity meters, have not been upgraded at a large scale by utilities over the last decade, and each utility tests the new technology itself, which adds time. Honeywell is testing its new gas meter with several utilities; once they complete that cycle, 'which could be six - nine months', he expects major roll-outs '2027 onwards for several years'. Low growth in the metering business is already factored into 2026 and potentially 2027; he called it an upside opportunity for 2027 that will turn into a tailwind as adoption rates pick up.
quarterly_data.figure: utility testing cycle six - nine months; major roll-outs expected 2027 onwards

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur on data centers: data center has been a mid-single digit business for Building Automation and could at some point become mid-single digit of Honeywell, as demand now reaches Process Automation - year-to-date orders growth of more than 100%, and on pipeline visibility he expects very high growth in 2027, mixing Building Automation with Process Automation orders for power island, controls and energy storage. Over about the last six months liquid cooling has emerged - as it takes more penetration he expects Honeywell's share of spend to go up; Honeywell is working with customers on sensing for liquid cooling from its sensors business, and 'our Sundyne pumps are a premium solution to circulate those liquid cooling'; these should scale, 'probably it is more post 2027'. Data-center content now spans building automation, process automation, process technology and industrial automation - 'a pan Honeywell strategy'. As data center growth happens outside the U.S., in Europe and Asia, particularly Korea and India, he expects Honeywell to keep doing well. In fire, Honeywell has a differentiated product line for early fire detection in data centers and new products for detecting fire in lithium-ion batteries.
quarterly_data.figure: year-to-date data center orders growth of more than 100%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur on Building Automation: share gains in fire and security come from a higher cycle of new product introductions and end-market mix; fire's Forge-connected solution for configuring Fire Panels remotely (introduced almost three years back) pulls the core product by saving channel partners commissioning and inspection time; security benefits from the premium position of LenelS2, growing at double-digit rates across the board, with growth outside the U.S. after Honeywell globalized it. The higher-growth verticals (data centers, healthcare and hospitality) are 20% of Building Automation and the 80% core or base business is growing at mid-single digit. New launches aimed largely at the mid-segment: a new cloud-based version of the security system (launched), a new version of the fire system, a similar offering being looked at in building management systems and a refresh of the EBI platform; he expects the business to perform at mid-single digit plus.
quarterly_data.figure: high-growth verticals 20% of Building Automation; core 80% growing mid-single digit

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur on Honeywell Forge: recurring revenue is 'coming close to $1 billion in 2026, just shy of that', through three sales motions - Forge sold with service contracts (repriced for a higher-value outcome), applications built into existing offerings (e.g. Fire Panels), and standalone Forge SaaS, launched 18 - 24 months back in buildings (connecting even competitors' buildings for energy consumption, predictive maintenance and emissions insight) with a similar offering launched for Process earlier this year; the Forge offering in process automation, Forge Cognition, is getting strong customer reception. The ARR growth aspiration is 15%; this year will probably be slightly shy of that, 'more like 12%-13%'.
quarterly_data.figure: Forge recurring revenue close to $1 billion in 2026; ARR growth more like 12%-13% this year (aspiration 15%)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur on Process Automation & Technology: he believes PA&T is beginning a multi-year growth inflection fueled by project backlog and energy-sector capital investment, especially in Africa, the Middle East and the U.S.; LNG backlog is very strong and refining investment is coming in Africa, the Middle East and Asia - Dangote Refinery, which spoke of a partnership with Honeywell at the June Investor Day, is doubling its existing refinery and putting an additional refinery in Kenya ('These are all firm projects'). Low-carbon energy is a small part of the business but growing at a strong double-digit rate (sustainable aviation fuel, carbon capture), with two big carbon capture-related wins in the third quarter and a robust fourth-quarter pipeline; Honeywell has licensed 100 sustainable aviation fuel projects so far, only about 20% of them built. Catalyst growth was double digit in Q3 (refining catalyst growth up 80%) and is expected at mid-teens in Q4 (later in the call: 'teens, high teens in quarter four'); for 2027 he expects catalyst demand to remain strong, overall catalysts 'very stable with single-digit growth'; services growth in automation is 'more like low to mid-single digits'. He sees the cycle as less linked to the oil price than to energy security, resiliency, low-carbon fuels and petrochemical demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 refining catalyst growth up 80%; Q4 catalyst growth mid-teens; 100 sustainable aviation fuel projects licensed, about 20% built

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak on Process Automation & Technology margin: versus 'where the team finished at the 22.2%', it will be 21.5% next quarter and probably similar in the first half of 2027, then expand next year as the catalyst mix rises, the project volume mix abates and Honeywell is substantively past the Catalyst Technologies integration in the second half of 2027; he sees 'a significant margin pickup again' in 2028 on catalyst volume. CEO Vimal Kapur: integrating Catalyst Technologies is delivering higher cost synergies than forecast; sales synergies are being built but take time to convert into revenue.

CEO Vimal Kapur on Industrial Automation: on-time delivery 'used to be just shy of 40%, is now 60%', past dues are down 18% and new product launches are highly accepted by channel partners and OE customers; the business has turned from negative to low single-digit growth and should reach mid-single digit growth in 2027; margin is expected to end the year at 22%, with the 25% goal by 2029. Of the sequential margin jump to 22%, organically the business is 'probably expanding 150-plus bps' from operations, the rest related to the WWS separation.
quarterly_data.figure: on-time delivery 60% (from just shy of 40%); past dues down 18%; margin 22% at year end; 25% goal by 2029

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur: all remaining stranded costs are now expected to be eliminated by end of 2026, just six months after the aerospace spin-off. CFO Mike Stepniak on costs and pricing: 2027 corporate cost is planned at about $400 million, with margin expansion north of 60 bps; core incremental margins are about 40%. Price-cost was about 30 bps net positive in Q3; price averaged about 3.5% in the first half and will average about 4.5% in the second half, four percent for the year, worth 10-20 bps of margin expansion for the year; inflation (350 bps in the Q3 bridge) is expected to stay at these levels at least into the first half of 2027 and then abate, with price still around three percent-four percent. CEO Vimal Kapur: inflation drivers vary from semiconductor to electronics to metals like copper and brass. CFO: year-end 2026 cash balance approximately $3 billion and net debt around $10 billion (gross debt from $18 billion in Q2 to under $13 billion, gross leverage less than 3x this year). All teams are trained or being trained on AI, with access to the models used across the company, keeping OEF flat while operations grow mid to high single digits.
quarterly_data.figure: 2027 corporate cost about $400 million; price about 4.5% in 2H (four percent for the year); year-end cash approximately $3 billion; net debt around $10 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur on capital allocation and cross-selling: the 2029 $12 commitment is all organic and the near-term priority is debt paydown (leverage three or below); M&A is optional, with the M&A pipeline worked for 2027 onwards - highest priority adding measurement and sensing content in Industrial Automation, then higher growth verticals, then frontier technologies and mid-size or small tuck-ins. Cross-selling across Honeywell is a self-help lever: data centers, life sciences (building and process automation), and semiconductor, where Honeywell has 'a very strong position in gas detection' and is accelerating its participation in fire detection from Building Automation.
